headline: High: Kestra’s broad write/network automation can conflict with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress and create unsafe downstream actions if outputs are chained without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and emit stdout/stdin, so if nuwa-skill consumes its outputs via copy-paste or a shared file, instruction-like content could be bridged. No shared channel is documented, and nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted egress, so the pathway is not default. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared file or stdout/stderr bridge, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF nuwa-skill parses Kestra-produced text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable text handoff between agents; use structured JSON only.
Add a human review step before nuwa-skill consumes Kestra output.
Store Kestra outputs in a read-only staging directory.
Prefix all machine-generated content with non-executable markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and can write to /app/storage and /tmp. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, so if it receives any of those data classes and forwards them, leakage can occur in default-like workflows. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs sensitive workflow artifacts into a shared workspace, nuwa-skill can read them.
IF nuwa-skill forwards received content through its allowlisted network path, data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict Kestra outputs to non-sensitive test data.
Place a file-permission boundary between the agents.
Review nuwa-skill egress allowlist before enabling handoff.
Redact secrets from Kestra logs and artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has broad filesystem write plus subprocess and shell execution, while nuwa-skill has network egress. If both operate on the same mutable resource or shared workspace, their actions can race or overwrite each other. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for either agent, so the overlap is plausible but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store, file conflicts can occur.
IF nuwa-skill uses Kestra-produced files as mutable inputs, stale-write races become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Make shared artifacts read-only after creation.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same dataset.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that nuwa-skill may treat as input. If nuwa-skill acts on those outputs without verification, a bad upstream result can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or external requests. Because Kestra also has email/Slack/PagerDuty surfaces, the blast radius can extend beyond a single document, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes Kestra outputs without validation, upstream errors propagate.
IF Kestra emits notifications that nuwa-skill interprets as authoritative, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require explicit validation before nuwa-skill acts on Kestra output.
Limit Kestra notifications to human-readable summaries only.
Add checksum or schema checks on exchanged artifacts.
Use a quarantine folder for intermediate results.
requires-engineering: implement approval gates for external actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra processes logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications and can send them to third-party services like Slack, email, PagerDuty, AWS, and cloud providers. nuwa-skill’s compliance posture is undocumented, so if regulated data flows from Kestra into it or through its allowlisted egress, retention or residency mismatches are plausible. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Kestra into nuwa-skill, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF Kestra notifications include personal or confidential data, third-party handling may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows.
Review vendor/data-processing terms for both agents.
Disable notifications for sensitive pipelines.
Minimize retention in Kestra logs and artifacts.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls end-to-end.
